_comment: The cross-family accounting model, machine-readable so the linter can
check the docs against it. This file DECLARES; it generates nothing --
a docs repo whose tables are codegen output makes every contributor
learn a build step and lets the generated copy drift from its source.
adapters = which CLI you drive. families = whose training produced the
output. They are not the same axis, and one adapter can serve several
families; the reviewer-pairing rule reads the FAMILY of the verified
families[].models = lowercase substrings of a model id that name its
family (roster.py): a leg whose model id names another family than the
one it declares, or a vendor in `unregistered`, is refused. An id that
names no family (a placeholder, a new model) passes, with a warning when
the declared family could be the accounting leg. A marker
inside another family's longer marker, both in the id, yields to it

codex.cli: codex (via its Claude Code companion plugin, or raw)

agy.note: two separate quota pools; the Claude pool is a legitimate cross-family reviewer for anything Claude did not write

opencode.note: free pool; catalogue changes, verify with `opencode models`. Kimi is reachable via the paid opencode-go/kimi-k3 pool, not the free one (opencode-runtime.md)

grok.note: paid pool, tier peer of codex/agy -- weekly shared quota on xAI plans; positioned by the owner 2026-08-13

cursor.note: paid pool, the widest adapter -- the pinned model decides the family; `auto` routes server-side and lands in unknown. Collisions to check when substituting: cursor gemini-* is the Gemini family (agy's), muse-spark is Meta and glm is GLM (opencode's), claude-* and gpt-* are the claude and codex adapters' families, and composer-2.5 / composer-2.5-fast are the Kimi family (owner ruling 2026-10-07) -- one family with any kimi-k3 leg, cursor's or opencode-go's, so the two cannot be two cross-family legs together

unregistered._comment: vendors whose models were seen (opencode-runtime.md, 2026-10-10) but whose family is not registered: a roster leg whose model id names one is refused, whatever family it declares or when it declares none

Gemini.note: Google. Gemma (e.g. openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free) is the same vendor's training and counts as Gemini: it adds no family and cannot stand in for a missing Gemini leg as a different one

Xiaomi.note: MiMo; native opencode free pool, e.g. opencode/mimo-v2.5-free

Tencent.note: Hunyuan, marketed as Hy3; native opencode free pool, e.g. opencode/hy3-free

Meta.note: marketed as Muse Spark; native opencode free pool, e.g. opencode/muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free

Kimi.note: Moonshot. Cursor composer-2.5 and composer-2.5-fast count as Kimi by the owner's ruling (2026-10-07): Cursor discloses that Composer 2.5 is built on Moonshot's Kimi K2.5 open checkpoint (continued pretraining plus RL; relayed by peers, not re-read here), so it is a DERIVATIVE -- weaker independence than a native Kimi -- and one family with every kimi-k3 leg (cursor kimi-k3-*, opencode-go/kimi-k3)

Qwen.note: Alibaba; opencode-go paid pool, e.g. opencode-go/qwen3.8-max (the review skill's top-tier judgement leg). Added 2026-09-25: the skill routed to it while this file did not know the family, so the accounting rule could not be applied to that leg

Meituan.note: LongCat; opencode-go paid pool, e.g. opencode-go/longcat-2.0

Composer.why: Cursor's in-house models OTHER than composer-2.5 and composer-2.5-fast (those two count as Kimi, see the Kimi family); the lineage of the rest is undisclosed, which is the stealth-model hazard again -- it might share any family's blind spots. Extra eyes, never the accounting leg

unknown.why: stealth models whose family is undisclosed by design; they might secretly share any family, so they can never SATISFY the cross-family rule -- fine as an additional pair of eyes, never the accounting leg
